chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Saffan ibn Yahya who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a sick man who arrives in Mecca but is unable to perform Tawaf around the House or go between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. He said: 'He is carried around (while being borne), his feet dragging on the ground until the ground touches his feet during the Tawaf. Then he is stopped at the beginning of As-Safa and Al-Marwah if he is still weak/ill.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a sick person who cannot walk during Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the fiqh of 'Tawaf bi-l-Haml' (carrying) for the incapacitated, emphasizing that the physical act of moving must be preserved through the dragging of feet to maintain the validity of the ritual. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle of facilitating religious obligations (Taysir) without compromising their essential form (Shakl), ensuring the pilgrim fulfills the duty despite physical limitation.
